sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: OpenHands Agent Canvas is a self-hosted control center for AI coding agents. It runs the open-source OpenHands agent and others like Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI, and lets you automate tasks that run on a schedule or from events in Slack, GitHub and Linear.
sixtySeconds.problem: Coding agents usually live in one terminal on one laptop and stop when it sleeps. Agent Canvas lets you run agents locally, in Docker, on VMs or in the cloud, switch between those backends, and turn routine work into automations.
whoFor: Developers who want a self-hosted agent workspace
Teams sharing an agent server for code review and dependency updates
People automating reports or issue triage
Users of Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or OpenCode
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it if you want an open-source, self-hosted hub for several agents with automations. Use the Docker option unless you're comfortable giving the agent full access to your filesystem.
requirements: Or Docker Desktop / Docker Engine (sandboxed option)
An API key for the LLM you want to use

overview: Agent Canvas is a developer control center for starting agent conversations and automating everyday tasks, like reports that publish to Slack. It runs locally by default and can connect to several agent backends, such as Docker containers, VMs or company infrastructure, with optional OpenHands Cloud or Enterprise.

It runs the open-source OpenHands agent out of the box and supports third-party agents through the Agent Client Protocol (ACP), including Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Pi and OpenCode. You can bring any LLM.

Automations integrate with Slack, GitHub, Linear, Notion and more, and run on a schedule or in response to webhooks. The README recommends running the backend on a cloud server so agents keep working when your laptop is closed, and has a self-hosting guide covering security hardening.

troubleshooting.solution: uid 10001 in the container needs read/write access to the workspace. On SELinux hosts, the bind mount may need a :z or :Z label.
Reuse the openhands-state volume; a fresh volume has no previous data.
